meta.name: pstack
meta.author: Lauren Tan (@poteto)
meta.tagline: if you want to go fast, go deep first. pstack helps you write less, but higher quality code. rigorous agent workflows you can parallelize with confidence.
meta.countDiscrepancies: flavio post says 24 skills/23 principles/22 playbooks (+1 internal); repo README/dir listing show 28 skills, 24 principles, 23 playbook files; marketplace shows 52 skills (=28+24) and 2 subagents.
meta.installClaude: /plugin marketplace add michael-denyer/pstack-claude  then  /plugin install pstack@pstack-claude  (commands are /pstack:<name>)

phases.name: Set up and route
phases.blurb: Install, pick models per role, then let poteto-mode route the task to a playbook. Guide chapters 1-2.

phases.name: Understand
phases.blurb: Read-only: how it works now, why it is shaped that way, what you were doing. Guide chapter 3.

phases.name: Design
phases.blurb: Settle shape before code: caller-first sketch, competing attempts, parallel coverage, adversarial review. Guide chapter 4.

phases.name: Build and clean
phases.blurb: Build playbooks (bug fix, feature, refactor, perf), then strip slop and comments before review. Guide chapter 5.

phases.name: Verify and review
phases.blurb: Prove behavior on the real artifact, vet numbers, attack the diff. Guide chapter 6.

phases.name: Ship
phases.blurb: Open a focused PR, drive it to merge-ready, verify independently, land the verified run. Guide chapter 6 (plus Babysit/Shipping playbooks).

phases.name: Run unattended
phases.blurb: Long autonomous work with a checkable finish condition and an auditable decision log. Guide chapter 7.

phases.name: Make it yours
phases.blurb: Capture lessons, fix repeated mistakes, personalise the mode. Guide chapter 9.

phases.name: Principles
phases.blurb: 24 one-rule skills (core, architecture, verification, delegation, meta). Indexed inline by poteto-mode; used to steer by name. Guide chapter 8.

skills.name: poteto-mode
skills.summary: Router and default entry point. Reads the principles index, matches the task to one of 23 playbooks, copies its steps verbatim into a todo list, calls specialist skills, delegates to subagents by model role, and writes unslopped replies.
skills.whenToUse: Any non-trivial or rigorous task; type it at the start of work (Cursor: option+enter makes it a sticky custom mode).
skills.whatItIs: The front door. It reads the rules, picks the right playbook for your task, and runs it with sub-agents and checks.
steps: Reads the principles index and matches your task to one of 23 playbooks
Copies that playbook's steps into a to-do list, word for word
Calls specialist skills (how, architect, swarm, interrogate, unslop...) as the playbook says
Sends code work to sub-agents, each with a set model, and reviews every diff itself
Writes the final reply in plain short sentences and names which principles changed a decision
behindTheScenes: Playbooks live in skills/poteto-mode/playbooks/*.md; helper scripts (watch-pr, orch, check-plan, worktree-audit) live in skills/poteto-mode/scripts
Uses the poteto-agent sub-agent type for ad-hoc helpers
Claude port: a SessionStart hook injects a reminder to use it when a task touches several files, a design choice, or an unknown bug
skills.output: The finished work plus a reply that says what changed, what was verified, and what is open.
skills.claudeCode: /pstack:poteto-mode (after /plugin install pstack@pstack-claude); or just say 'use poteto-mode to...'. A SessionStart hook reminds Claude to use it.
skills.codex: Codex: ships a native port (codex plugin add pstack@pstack-claude); skills are the same SKILL.md files, ask for it by name (Codex shortcuts optional). Needs multi_agent for fan-out. Codex: same skill; hook runs after you trust it via /hooks. Skills-only install: ask for poteto-mode by name or add a line to AGENTS.md.

skills.name: setup-pstack
skills.summary: Detects available models, asks for a reasoning budget, writes a per-role model rule (Cursor: ~/.cursor/rules/pstack-models.mdc). Offers to generate a verification skill at the end.
skills.whenToUse: Once after install, and whenever you want to change models/effort per role. Claude Code: /pstack:setup-pstack; also toggles the routing hook.
skills.whatItIs: Picks which AI model pstack uses for each job (code, judgment, reviews) and how hard it thinks.
steps: Lists the models your session can actually use
Loads your current choices, or the defaults
Asks for a budget (small, medium, large, unlimited) and fills in a model per role
Shows every role and lets you change any of them
Checks each model name is real, then writes the settings file
Offers to build a project verification skill if you have none
behindTheScenes: Writes ~/.cursor/rules/pstack-models.mdc in Cursor (always-applied rule); the Claude port writes a model sheet you add to CLAUDE.md with an @ line
Every other pstack skill reads these role lines before it spawns a sub-agent
Claude port also asks if the SessionStart routing hook stays on
skills.output: A settings file that sets the model per role; applies to new sessions.
skills.codex: Codex: ships a native port (codex plugin add pstack@pstack-claude); skills are the same SKILL.md files, ask for it by name (Codex shortcuts optional). Needs multi_agent for fan-out. Codex: setup-pstack has its own Codex sheet path; use your Codex model names (codex-tools.md).

skills.name: poteto-help
skills.summary: Guided help: finds out what you are trying to do, answers, hands you a prompt to send and links the skill/guide page. Does not start the work.
skills.whenToUse: New to pstack or unsure which skill, playbook or principle fits. Runs only when typed.
skills.whatItIs: A guide that answers questions about pstack and hands you a prompt to send.
steps: Works out what you need: set up, start a task, pick a skill, fix a bad run, or customize
Checks if your model settings file exists
Reads the right guide file before quoting it
Replies with the answer, a copy-ready prompt, and a link to the source file
behindTheScenes: Reads references/recipes.md and references/prompting.md plus the docs/guide pages
Does not start the work itself; you send the prompt
skills.output: An answer, a prompt you can send, and a link.
skills.codex: Codex: ships a native port (codex plugin add pstack@pstack-claude); skills are the same SKILL.md files, ask for it by name (Codex shortcuts optional). Needs multi_agent for fan-out.

skills.name: figure-it-out
skills.summary: Designs a bespoke, auditable playbook when no bundled one fits (large migration, ambitious multi-part change, work reviewed after stepping away). Scales rigor, runs a hypothesis loop, logs decisions.
skills.whenToUse: No narrower playbook fits, or the work is large/cross-cutting or will be reviewed later.
skills.whatItIs: Designs a custom playbook when your job is too big or odd for the standard ones.
steps: Frame: writes the done-condition as something checkable, sizes the work, sets how strict to be
Design: splits work into small units, riskiest first, and builds the check before the work
Runs a loop per unit: hypothesis, smallest change, measure on the real thing, keep or revert
Logs every decision as it goes
Checks the whole result against the done-condition on the real product
behindTheScenes: Runs architect (which runs arena) for one-way-door design choices
Logs through show-me-your-work
Each worker gets its own worktree or branch
skills.output: The playbook it designed, the decision trail path, what is verified, what is still open.
skills.codex: Codex: ships a native port (codex plugin add pstack@pstack-claude); skills are the same SKILL.md files, ask for it by name (Codex shortcuts optional). Needs multi_agent for fan-out.

skills.name: how
skills.summary: Explains how a subsystem works now: concepts, runtime flow, files, sharp edges. Narrow question uses one explainer; large subsystems split into 2-4 explorers plus an explainer. Also placement/ownership questions.
skills.whenToUse: Before changing unfamiliar code; "how does X work", "where should this live".
skills.whatItIs: Explains how a part of the code works, like onboarding a new senior engineer.
steps: Decides if the question is simple (one file) or complex (a subsystem)
Simple: one explainer sub-agent reads the code and writes the answer
Complex: splits the question into 2-4 angles and runs one read-only explorer per angle at once
Then one explainer turns all the findings into the write-up
Shows it with light edits only
behindTheScenes: All sub-agents are read-only generalPurpose Task calls
Prompts come from references/explorer-prompt.md and explainer-prompt.md
Models come from the 'how explorer' and 'how explainer' lines in your settings
skills.output: An explanation: Overview, Key Concepts, How It Works, Where Things Live, Gotchas.
skills.codex: Codex: ships a native port (codex plugin add pstack@pstack-claude); skills are the same SKILL.md files, ask for it by name (Codex shortcuts optional). Needs multi_agent for fan-out. Codex: explorers map to spawn_agent; turn on multi_agent in ~/.codex/config.toml or it runs as one pass.

skills.name: why
skills.summary: Historical evidence for why code has its shape. Discovers MCPs at run time and queries seven evidence categories in parallel (source control, issues, docs, chat, infra observability, error tracking, analytics); separates fact from inference and reports empty searches.
skills.whenToUse: Design rationale, regressions, postmortems, data-backed thresholds.
skills.whatItIs: Finds the reasons behind code: who decided, what forced it, and what we only guess.
steps: Pins down the code you mean and what you are asking
Builds an anchor: git blame, git log, PR numbers, and PR bodies via gh
Finds which tools are connected (git, tickets, docs, chat, monitoring, errors, analytics)
Runs one investigator per source at once; each owns one tool
One synthesizer merges the findings and keeps facts apart from guesses
Presents the cited result, with a Preserve/Change/Avoid/Risk list if you plan to change it
behindTheScenes: Investigators run in agent mode (not read-only) so they can use MCP tools
Prompts and rules: references/epistemics.md, investigator-prompt.md, synthesizer-prompt.md, sources/*.md
Missing sources are listed as gaps, not skipped quietly
skills.output: A cited report: what we found, what we infer, competing ideas, what we don't know, confidence.
skills.codex: Codex: ships a native port (codex plugin add pstack@pstack-claude); skills are the same SKILL.md files, ask for it by name (Codex shortcuts optional). Needs multi_agent for fan-out. Codex: lists MCP servers from the tools Codex exposes; sub-agents map to spawn_agent.

skills.name: teach
skills.summary: Runs how + why and weaves one plain explanation, built up diagram by diagram.
skills.whenToUse: You want to genuinely understand a change or subsystem, not just a summary.
skills.whatItIs: Explains a piece of work in plain words so you really understand it.
steps: Picks the few things you should walk away knowing, from what you asked and what you already know
Runs how and why in parallel and blends the results
Starts with a plain definition, then ties it to your code
Builds diagrams one part at a time instead of one big picture
Stays a conversation: smallest full answer first, goes deeper when you ask
behindTheScenes: Calls the how and why skills for the real digging
Writes through unslop
Keeps why's hedging words as they are
skills.output: A plain explanation, not a report about what it did.
skills.codex: Codex: ships a native port (codex plugin add pstack@pstack-claude); skills are the same SKILL.md files, ask for it by name (Codex shortcuts optional). Needs multi_agent for fan-out. Codex: how+why in parallel map to spawn_agent; image generation uses the Codex equivalent.

skills.name: recall
skills.summary: Rebuilds your recent context on a topic from your own chat transcripts, live git/PR state and the shared record; returns a tight current-state brief.
skills.whenToUse: Starting or resuming work after days away ("catch me up").
skills.whatItIs: Rebuilds what you were working on from your chat history and the team record, then hands back a short brief.
steps: Locks scope: time window (default last 7 days), topic, current workspace
Fans out cheap sub-agents over your past chat transcripts, grep topic first
Runs why's investigators on tickets, chat, docs and errors for the same topic
Checks every PR, branch and ticket it found with git and gh
Writes a brief: capsule, tagged threads, problems, one next move
behindTheScenes: Reads transcripts at ~/.cursor/projects/<slug>/agent-transcripts/
Never reads another project's transcripts unless asked
Raw transcripts stay in sub-agents; the main chat gets only findings
skills.output: A short brief with status tags like [merged #N] or [open PR #N] and a next step.
skills.codex: Codex: ships a native port (codex plugin add pstack@pstack-claude); skills are the same SKILL.md files, ask for it by name (Codex shortcuts optional). Needs multi_agent for fan-out. Codex: transcript paths in the source are Cursor's; Codex layout not covered in the sources (inference).

skills.name: ketchup
skills.summary: Catches you up on everything in this chat since your last message, in plain words, with an executive summary per action item.
skills.whenToUse: Returning to a long agent chat and needing to make the calls.
skills.whatItIs: Catches you up on this chat since your last message, in plain words, and lists what only you can decide.
steps: Finds your last real message (not notifications or sub-agent reports)
Collects your own work, sub-agent reports, and others' messages since then
Checks the live state of each PR, CI run, or agent
Opens with the count of action items, then what happened, most important first
Gives each action item a short summary: the decision, options, recommendation, what happens if you wait
behindTheScenes: Read-only turn
Uses the plain voice of /bro
skills.output: A short catch-up plus action items.
skills.claudeCode: Not in the Claude Code port (Cursor repo only).
skills.codex: Not in the Claude or Codex ports (Cursor repo only per the repo listings).

skills.name: bro
skills.summary: Restates the last message in plain human language with no jargon.
skills.whenToUse: The answer is right but unreadable.
skills.whatItIs: Says the last message again in simple human words.
steps: Takes the agent's last message
Drops the jargon
Restates it shorter and plainer
behindTheScenes: The whole skill is three sentences; no sub-agents, no files
skills.output: A plain-language rewrite.
skills.codex: Codex: ships a native port (codex plugin add pstack@pstack-claude); skills are the same SKILL.md files, ask for it by name (Codex shortcuts optional). Needs multi_agent for fan-out. Codex: plain SKILL.md, so it should load the same (inference).

skills.name: architect
skills.summary: Five phases: ground (runs how, maybe why), sketch several shapes starting from caller usage, optional checkpoint ("with checkpoint"), implement against the sketch, scrap the sketch if repeated friction proves it wrong.
skills.whenToUse: Code that crosses a function boundary; before locking in types/signatures/module shape.
skills.whatItIs: Sketches the types, function signatures and module layout first, then fills in code against that sketch.
steps: Ground: runs how (and why if ownership changes) on the systems it touches
Sketch: runs arena with at least two structurally different designs
Screens each candidate against a design red-flags list and prefers the smaller interface
Agree: no pause by default; pauses only if you ask for a checkpoint
Implement: replaces 'not implemented' bodies; surprises are reported, not hidden
Scrap: if the same workaround keeps appearing, throws the sketch out and redesigns
behindTheScenes: Runners come from the 'architect runners' setting
Reads references/design-red-flags.md, runner-prompt.md, rationale-template.md
Writes the usage sketch first, then types; ships a rationale file next to it
skills.output: A type/signature sketch (or module map) plus a rationale with the synthesis decision.
skills.codex: Codex: ships a native port (codex plugin add pstack@pstack-claude); skills are the same SKILL.md files, ask for it by name (Codex shortcuts optional). Needs multi_agent for fan-out. Codex: the arena fan-out maps to spawn_agent.

skills.name: arena
skills.summary: Same brief to N models, each in its own worktree; private rubric, cross-model judge, coordinator reads all and picks a base and grafts the best parts from others.
skills.whenToUse: One attempt at a non-trivial artifact would lock in the wrong shape; design/code bakeoffs.
skills.whatItIs: Runs several agents on the same task, picks the best result, and borrows the good parts from the rest.
steps: Frame: states the artifact, writes a 3-6 point rubric, picks runners, gives each its own folder or worktree
Fan out: all candidates start in one message, in the background
Cross-judge: one read-only judge on a different model family scores them
Pick: you read every candidate end to end and choose a base
Graft: port one or two strong ideas from each loser, by hand
Verify the final result like any other output
behindTheScenes: Runners and judge come from the 'arena runners' and 'arena cross-judge pool' settings
Candidates only see the task; the rubric is for the judge
Fewer than all candidates is fine; dropouts are noted
skills.output: One merged result plus a note on the base, the grafts, and the verification.
skills.codex: Codex: ships a native port (codex plugin add pstack@pstack-claude); skills are the same SKILL.md files, ask for it by name (Codex shortcuts optional). Needs multi_agent for fan-out. Codex: candidates and judge map to spawn_agent; use your own Codex models.

skills.name: swarm
skills.summary: Fans out N parallel workers across independent slices or declared race arms, drains them, returns one report (each worker PASS / ISSUES / BLOCKED with evidence).
skills.whenToUse: Coverage matrices, races, gauntlets, exploration partitions (vs arena = competing attempts at one thing).
skills.whatItIs: Runs many workers at once on slices, races, or comparisons, and returns one report.
steps: Frame: states done-condition, shape (slices, race, or both), count, and worker model
Fan out: starts all workers in one message in the cloud, in the background
Each worker reports PASS, ISSUES, or BLOCKED with evidence
Aggregate: drops results missing required SHAs or method, retries once, then records a gap
Report: one table, one-line issues, gaps
behindTheScenes: Workers are generalPurpose with environment 'cloud' (local only if they need your machine)
Model from the 'swarm workers' setting
Writers get their own output folder or worktree
skills.output: One table of results, evidenced issues, and any gaps.
skills.codex: Codex: ships a native port (codex plugin add pstack@pstack-claude); skills are the same SKILL.md files, ask for it by name (Codex shortcuts optional). Needs multi_agent for fan-out. Codex: each worker is a spawn_agent call; no separate background flag needed.

skills.name: interrogate
skills.summary: Multi-model adversarial review: same diff, intent and rules to several models; lead merges findings into act on / consider / noted / dismissed. Includes a strict code-quality lens. Never applies changes automatically.
skills.whenToUse: A diff is ready to attack; contested design before shipping. Claude port: three models.
skills.whatItIs: Several different AI models try to tear your change apart; you get one judged verdict.
steps: Scopes the diff or files (git diff main...HEAD on a branch)
Writes the intent in one paragraph; asks if unsure
Starts one read-only reviewer per model at the same time
Merges findings, noting which models raised each
Sorts them into Act on, Consider, Noted, Dismissed with reasons
Never applies changes itself
behindTheScenes: Prompt from references/reviewer-prompt.md, rubric.md, code-quality-review.md; lead role from lead-judgment.md
Reviewer list comes from the 'interrogate reviewers' setting
Issues two models found separately are the strongest signal
skills.output: An intent, reviewers, four finding buckets, and an agreement map.
skills.codex: Codex: ships a native port (codex plugin add pstack@pstack-claude); skills are the same SKILL.md files, ask for it by name (Codex shortcuts optional). Needs multi_agent for fan-out. Codex: dispatch fields map to spawn_agent; keep the panel model-diverse.

skills.name: tdd
skills.summary: Failing test first, then the fix.
skills.whenToUse: Only when asked, or the bug has an obvious cheap local test path.
skills.whatItIs: Writes a failing test for a bug first, then fixes it. Skips the test when it would be a bad one.
steps: Works out intended vs current behavior and the smallest reproduction
Picks the narrowest existing test style for that code
Writes the smallest failing test
Runs it to see it fail for the right reason
Makes the smallest fix, then reruns the test
behindTheScenes: No files besides the test and the fix
If a test is impractical it uses a script, browser run or log check instead
Final reply names the failing-before and passing-after evidence
skills.output: A regression test plus before/after proof.
skills.codex: Codex: ships a native port (codex plugin add pstack@pstack-claude); skills are the same SKILL.md files, ask for it by name (Codex shortcuts optional). Needs multi_agent for fan-out. Codex: plain SKILL.md (inference).

skills.name: typescript-best-practices
skills.summary: Grounds the type-system-discipline principle in TypeScript syntax; path-scoped to **/*.ts and **/*.tsx.
skills.whenToUse: Reading or editing .ts/.tsx.
skills.whatItIs: A rule sheet for typed TypeScript: no casts, no loose types, check data at the edges.
steps: Applies type-system-discipline first
Uses discriminated unions, branded types, unknown instead of any
Parses outside data once at the boundary
Uses exhaustive checks (never) so new cases break the build
Prefers real tests over mocks and structured logs over console.log
behindTheScenes: Has a paths filter for **/*.ts and **/*.tsx so it applies to those files
Examples are in references/patterns.md
skills.output: TypeScript that follows the rule table.
skills.codex: Codex: ships a native port (codex plugin add pstack@pstack-claude); skills are the same SKILL.md files, ask for it by name (Codex shortcuts optional). Needs multi_agent for fan-out. Codex: path-based auto-load is a Claude/Cursor frontmatter feature; Codex support not stated (inference).

skills.name: unslop
skills.summary: Removes AI tells from any writing. Marked "must always apply" and used on every prose surface including poteto-mode replies.
skills.whenToUse: Any prose: replies, docs, PR text.
skills.whatItIs: Strips the usual AI-sounding habits from any writing.
steps: Scans for numbered patterns: AI vocabulary, em dashes, filler, hedging, fake 'not just X but Y'
Rewrites each hit in plain words
Keeps the meaning and the tone
Prefers active voice and whole sentences
behindTheScenes: poteto-mode runs it on every reply; the description says it must always apply
Other skills cite its rule numbers (for example, rule 14 on colons)
skills.output: The same text without AI tells.
skills.codex: Codex: ships a native port (codex plugin add pstack@pstack-claude); skills are the same SKILL.md files, ask for it by name (Codex shortcuts optional). Needs multi_agent for fan-out. Codex: plain SKILL.md (inference).

skills.name: technical-writing
skills.summary: Layered doc standard: Diataxis structure, Google developer style, Simplified Technical English, Global English.
skills.whenToUse: Docs, RFCs, READMEs, PR descriptions, commit messages.
skills.whatItIs: A writing standard for docs, READMEs, RFCs, PR descriptions and commit messages.
steps: Picks one mode first: tutorial, how-to, reference, or explanation
Writes direct sentences to the reader in present tense
Splits long instructions: one step per sentence
Removes anything that could be read two ways
Varies sentence length so it does not read machine-written
behindTheScenes: Layers four standards: Diataxis, Google developer style, Simplified Technical English, Global English
poteto-mode calls it for docs and PR descriptions
skills.output: Docs that follow one clear mode.
skills.codex: Codex: ships a native port (codex plugin add pstack@pstack-claude); skills are the same SKILL.md files, ask for it by name (Codex shortcuts optional). Needs multi_agent for fan-out. Codex: plain SKILL.md (inference).

skills.name: no-comments
skills.summary: Spawns the Comment Sicko subagent to strip comments, fixes accepted findings, offers to encode "do not remove" constraints as a type, runtime check, test or lint.
skills.whenToUse: Before review.
skills.whatItIs: Deletes needless code comments and fixes the code that needed them.
steps: Takes your files or the diff against main
Spawns the Comment Sicko sub-agent to flag and delete comments
Checks its work and restores any deletion that was wrong
Fixes flagged code directly, or runs architect once if a new shape is needed
Offers a lint, type or test to replace 'do not remove' comments
Reports deletions, restores and open items
behindTheScenes: Uses the comment-sicko agent (agents/comment-sicko.md)
Comment Sicko only edits comments, never application code
Can call how/why on a suspicious comment
skills.output: A cleaner diff plus a report.
skills.codex: Codex: ships a native port (codex plugin add pstack@pstack-claude); skills are the same SKILL.md files, ask for it by name (Codex shortcuts optional). Needs multi_agent for fan-out. Codex: no comment-sicko agent type; spawn_agent reads the agent file first.

skills.name: deslop
skills.summary: Removes AI-generated code slop and cleans up style. In the Cursor original it lives in the separate cursor-team-kit plugin; bundled in the Claude port.
skills.whenToUse: Before commit.
skills.note: Cursor original: ships in cursor-team-kit, not pstack. Claude port bundles it (imported from cursor-team-kit).
skills.whatItIs: Removes the leftovers AI code tends to add, on the current diff.
steps: Checks the diff against main
Removes extra comments, odd try/catch, 'any' casts, deep nesting
Keeps behavior unchanged
Gives a 1-3 sentence summary
behindTheScenes: No scripts or sub-agents; it is a short checklist
poteto-mode runs it before commit (from the cursor-team-kit plugin in Cursor)
skills.output: A leaner diff and a short summary.
skills.codex: Codex: ships a native port (codex plugin add pstack@pstack-claude); skills are the same SKILL.md files, ask for it by name (Codex shortcuts optional). Needs multi_agent for fan-out. Codex: plain SKILL.md (inference).

skills.name: create-verification-skill
skills.summary: Inspects the repo and writes a project-local verify-<app> skill (launch, health check, drive behavior, capture evidence, clean up) plus a feature map; runs it once before handing over. Poteto: "critical infrastructure".
skills.whenToUse: Project has no scripted way to prove app behavior.
skills.trigger: no way to test the app
skills.whatItIs: Builds a project skill that lets future agents run your app like a user and capture proof.
steps: Interviews the repo (not you) for surface, run command, drive method, evidence, isolation
Writes verify-<app>/SKILL.md with Launch, Doctor, Drive, Evidence, Cleanup, Helpers
Seeds a features/ folder with one file per user feature
Runs its own instructions once end to end
Points you to maintain-verification-skill
behindTheScenes: Writes .cursor/skills/verify-<app>/ in Cursor (the Codex note says a different project-skill location is used)
Cleanup never deletes the proof it captured
skills.output: A tested project-local verify skill with a feature map.
skills.codex: Codex: ships a native port (codex plugin add pstack@pstack-claude); skills are the same SKILL.md files, ask for it by name (Codex shortcuts optional). Needs multi_agent for fan-out. Codex: write it to Codex's project-skill location.

skills.name: maintain-verification-skill
skills.summary: Periodic pass: parallel source readers per feature, one live session driving every feature, at most one PR of proven corrections. Cannot hide a product bug by editing docs.
skills.whenToUse: Verify skill / feature map has drifted from the app (poteto suggests a daily routine).
skills.whatItIs: Checks a verify skill against the real app and fixes drift in one PR.
steps: Finds the verify skill and tidies its feature index
Source wave: one read-only sub-agent per feature
Reconciles the findings and sweeps recent changes for missing features
Live pass: drives every feature in the real app
Triage: doc drift, harness gap, or product bug
Ships one PR, or reports clean/blocked
behindTheScenes: Only edits the verify skill's own folder, never product code
skills.output: Outcome clean, changed (one PR) or blocked.
skills.codex: Codex: ships a native port (codex plugin add pstack@pstack-claude); skills are the same SKILL.md files, ask for it by name (Codex shortcuts optional). Needs multi_agent for fan-out. Codex: per-feature readers map to spawn_agent.

skills.name: benchmark-checklist
skills.summary: Vets a measurement before you report it: limiter, tuning, limits, errors, repeatability, relevance, whether the work happened.

principlesHowItWorks: Each of the 24 principles is its own small skill (skills/principle-<name>/SKILL.md) with disable-model-invocation: true, so it is not picked up by name matching on its own.
poteto-mode lists all 24 inline with a one-line 'when it applies' trigger. This is the index it reads at the start of every multi-step task.
When a trigger fits, the agent must read that principle's full SKILL.md, apply it, and name it in its reply with the decision it changed. It may only cite principles it read this session.
Other skills and playbooks call principles by name too (architect cites exhaust-the-design-space, refactoring cites subtract-before-you-add, bug-fix cites sequence-verifiable-units).
You do not run them as commands. You can steer with the name: 'use subtract before you add' points the agent at a rule it has already read (docs/guide/08-principles.md).
They are separate from the workflow skills: workflows say what steps to run; principles say what judgment to apply while running them.
